Topics · The holy books together

Was Abraham a Jew, a Christian or a Muslim?

Three communities call Abraham their father. The Quran asks what came before him and after.

Part 1 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ لِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ فِىٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَتِ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةُ وَٱلْإِنجِيلُ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦٓ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Then will you not reason?

Quran · Aal Imran 3:65

Three communities love this man, each with good reason. Jews call him our father and carry his covenant in the body. Christians call him the father of all who believe. Muslims turn each day toward the house whose foundations he raised. Test the claims by one checkable fact. The Torah came after him, the Gospel later still. The verse asks how a man can belong to what came after him. The same test falls on the Quran, the latest of the three, and it does not spare Muslims.

A question for you

What did Abraham have, before any of these books existed?

If you sayA covenant with God
ThenThen the covenant was made with a man who had no Torah, no Temple and no name for his community. The next verse names what he had.
If you sayFaith, and nothing else yet
ThenPaul is with you, and many Christians. The next verse gives that faith a shape: a whole turning toward God.
If you sayAn obedience the Torah would later spell out
ThenSo the Talmud reports the sages saying. Then he had the substance, and the written law came after. The next verse asks what that substance was.

Part 2 of 3

﴿مَا كَانَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ يَهُودِيًّا وَلَا نَصْرَانِيًّا وَلَـٰكِن كَانَ حَنِيفًا مُّسْلِمًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim [submitting to Allāh]. And he was not of the polytheists.[129]

Translator's notes

[129] Those who associate others with Allāh.

Quran · Aal Imran 3:67

Translation

The princes of the peoples are gathered together, the people of the God of Abraham. For the shields of the earth belong to God. He is greatly exalted!

Original · Hebrew

נְדִ֘יבֵ֤י עַמִּ֨ים ׀ נֶאֱסָ֗פוּ עַם֮ אֱלֹהֵ֪י אַבְרָ֫הָ֥ם כִּ֣י לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים מָֽגִנֵּי־אֶ֗רֶץ מְאֹ֣ד נַעֲלָֽה׃

the Psalms · 47:9

World English Bible

﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥٓ أَسْلِمْ ۖ قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted [in Islām][45] to the Lord of the worlds."

Translator's notes

[45] The meaning of the word "Islām" is "submission to the will of Allāh." This is the way of life ordained by Allāh and taught by all of the prophets from Adam to Muḥammad (ﷺ). A Muslim is one who submits himself to Allāh.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:131

Translation

Abram fell on his face. God talked with him, saying,

Original · Hebrew

וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַבְרָ֖ם עַל־פָּנָ֑יו וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 17:3

World English Bible

The verse removes all three as labels and says what he was: hanif, muslim. The first means one who has turned from everything else toward God. The second means surrendered. A sharp reader will say: you dropped two names and kept your own. That is a fair objection. The answer lies in the second verse, where the word is an act: God says surrender, and Abraham says I have surrendered. That is what he did, in any language. The Arabic word and the claim are the Quran's.

A question for you

Which word would you choose for what Abraham did?

If you sayFaith
ThenThen the question is what faith does. Abraham's faith had feet: it left home and walked. The Arabic word in the verse names that same departure.
If you sayObedience
ThenAnd it was obedience to God alone, before any written law existed. That makes it a root shared by all who came after.
If you saySurrender
ThenThen you have used the verse's own word in your own tongue, as a description of an act and no membership. That is how the verse uses it, and it belongs to whoever does it.

Part 3 of 3

﴿إِنَّ أَوْلَى ٱلنَّاسِ بِإِبْرَٰهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ وَهَـٰذَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَلِىُّ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among the people are those who followed him [in submission to Allāh] and this prophet [i.e., Muḥammad (ﷺ)] and those who believe [in his message]. And Allāh is the Ally[130] of the believers.

Translator's notes

[130] Refer to footnote in verse 2:257.

Quran · Aal Imran 3:68

﴿تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ ۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُم مَّا كَسَبْتُمْ ۖ وَلَا تُسْـَٔلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

That was a nation which has passed on. It will have [the consequence of] what it earned, and you will have what you have earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:134

Translation

Don’t think to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father,’ for I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ μὴ δόξητε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 3:9

World English Bible

If labels do not decide, what does? The verse gives the measure of closeness: those nearest to Abraham are those who followed him. It then names this Prophet and the believers, which is the Quran's own claim, and a Jew or a Christian need not grant it. The second verse speaks to everyone: that was a community now gone, with what it earned, and you have what you earned. Each answers for their own deeds. That includes the reader of this page, Muslim or not.

A question for you

By what measure would you call someone a child of Abraham?

If you sayDescent
ThenDescent is real, the Torah and the Quran honour it, and the verse does not erase it. It asks only what descent gives by itself, and its answer is that each has what each has earned.
If you sayA faith like his
ThenThat is Paul's measure. The verse says those who followed him, so faith and following are one movement here.
If you sayDoing what he did
ThenJohn's Gospel reports this measure from Jesus, the sages hold it, and so does the verse. It cannot be claimed, only done.
